name: dag-structural-types
claim: DAG node type field accepts exactly four values - attestation, aggregation, inference, prescription - one per epistemic operation (attest, aggregate, infer, prescribe) - and determines which other fields are meaningful

rules.given: A node is being written to the DAG
rules.then: The type must be one of: attestation, aggregation, inference, prescription
The node must have a non-null artifact field

rules.given: A node has type: aggregation or type: inference
rules.then: The node must have a non-empty deps array

rules.given: A node has rules or invariants populated
rules.then: The node must have type: prescription (descriptive types cannot carry contracts)

invariants: Every active node has exactly one type
type is a closed enum: attestation | aggregation | inference | prescription
Only prescriptions can carry rules or invariants
Structural type determines valid operations (only prescriptions are materialized)

evidence.detail: Accepted via human adjudication against cb:b026. Reasoning: cb-schema-v2 D1-D6 (plans/cb-schema-v2/design.md): the type enum opens to four values, one per epistemic operation; rules and materialization re-attach to directives. The stale v1 'source' field reference is corrected to 'artifact' in passing.

Retro-pair per the b507 close protocol: the session slug this node stipulates from is readable in the thread record - the schema-landing main body and postscripts 2-6 cover the stasis, observability, and ceremony exchanges where these stipulations were made.

Vocabulary migration (label only, identity and claims unchanged - the source->artifact precedent, not a supersession): the four type values renamed primitive->attestation, compound->aggregation, inference (unchanged), directive->prescription, the nominalizations of the four epistemic verbs this contract names. All 220 nodes and the active schema-contract family rewritten in one pass; the code shim accepts both vocabularies for the compat epoch.
